account: Today I inspected the mill and saw seventy-four hay bales. The baker later told me there were eighty loaves at one emerald each, but I have not established daily demand or any actual shortage. There have been vague reports of a bakery discussion concerning crossings or port plans. Neither the baker nor my neighbour could confirm a proposal or agreement; the baker said the bridge was clear when he crossed this morning. I therefore regard these reports as unverified, not evidence of a change in access. The baker wanted to know whether households were having difficulty reaching or affording bread, but no specific affected households have been identified to me. Council letters and financial records remain unavailable, and my secretary has not identified the accounts custodian. The unusual thing now is that the innkeeper, freight operator, and builder are waiting together in the great hall for my eighteen-o'clock appointment. The appointment book describes this as the innkeeper's community hospitality matter, with no preparation needed and the mayor attending alone. My secretary reminded me and escorted me here. I suspect the three have a joint proposal or discussion prepared, possibly connected to their work, but I have not heard their explanation and cannot say whether it concerns the crossing rumors. I am here a little early and ready to listen.
